title: I Read Every Page of Nvidia's Latest Investor Update | NVDA Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc reads every page of Nvidia's Q3 investor update and says it was better than feared after Jensen Huang's forced resignation. The overlooked detail is token demand: OpenRouter weekly token volume is up 35x year over year and 3.5x in three months, agentic workloads are about 80% of tokens, and token prices are down nearly 60% since May. GPU rental prices are rising - Hopper recontracted at up to twice the original price, B300 up more than 60% since introduction - and Nvidia compute is fully utilized and sold out at every hyperscaler and neocloud. That makes GPUs appreciating collateral, easing financing of data-centre builds by CoreWeave, Nebius, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle. Consumer agentic AI (Meta's Muse agent, 10M+ downloads in the US and Canada) has not hit demand yet. Risks: leadership - Jensen is irreplaceable and innovation risk bites from 2029 - plus the SEC and board investigation overhang. Valuation: forward P/E 9.8 against roughly 75% revenue growth forecast, over 60% operating and over 70% gross margins. His DCF fair value is $259 (from $260). Call: NVDA BUY reiterated at about $150 stated - stale, since NVDA closed Friday 20 Nov at $125.53 - back in his top-10 stocks to buy; he owns it and may add more.

He owns it (one of largest positions), is interested in adding more, and upgraded NVDA back into his top-10 stocks to buy. Not a flip: last explicit call BUY 19 Nov (20 Nov video was an UNCERTAIN passing mention only). Note: his stated ~$150 is stale - NVDA closed Fri 20 Nov at $125.53, down 14%.
calls.base_case: Demand exceeds supply into 2027 as consumer agentic AI (Meta's Muse agent, 10M+ downloads) adds to enterprise demand; GPU resale values holding/rising eases financing for data-centre buyers.
calls.bull_case: Token volumes keep compounding and supply unlocks; single-digit forward P/E re-rates.
